context_requirements: Functional muscarinic acetylcholine receptors (CHRM1/CHRM3) coupled to Gq/PLC signaling
An autocrine or paracrine cholinergic stimulus to provide basal receptor activity
Cell types in which muscarinic signaling drives transcriptional programs (e.g., neurons, some epithelial/secretory cells)
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines
Enrichment of a cholinergic or Gq-coupled transcriptional signature after treatment
Changes that are reversed by co-treatment with a muscarinic agonist

evidence.supports: Muscarinic cholinergic receptor antagonism by scopolamine produces rapid antidepressant effects in humans, indicating that CHRM1/CHRM3 blockade can have physiological consequences, but the relevant transcriptional response is likely confined to specific CNS contexts.
